title: Hear From Us: Skits & Focus
topic: Bar graphs, categorical data, interpreting data displays

items.prompt: In the Human Bar Graph activity, each student's position represents:

choices.A: A random spot with no meaning
choices.B: A data value for a category, with more students forming taller groups

items.rationale: In a human bar graph, group size (how many students stand in a line) represents frequency, just like bar height in a bar graph.

items.prompt: The Keep-or-Rid class vote had these tallies: Keep = 18, Rid = 24. How many students voted in total?
Using the same vote (Keep = 18, Rid = 24), which category received more votes?
A bar graph is most useful for displaying:

choices.A: How one value changes continuously over time
choices.B: The frequency of items across different categories
choices.C: Every individual data point in exact detail

items.rationale: Bar graphs compare frequencies or amounts across separate categories.

items.prompt: Using Keep = 18, Rid = 24 (42 total votes), what percent of votes were "Rid"? Round to the nearest whole percent.
